test_title: PYST 66: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 26 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following methods will conserve natural forest cover and various forest products?
solution:
The correct answer is __**वनीकरण को बढ़ावा देना**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Afforestation (वनीकरण)** is the process of planting trees on land that has not recently been covered by forest, or was never a forest. It is a proactive method to increase **green cover** and ensure the **conservation** of natural ecosystems. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Deforestation (वनों की कटाई)** refers to the permanent removal of trees to make room for something besides forest. This process leads to **habitat loss**, **soil erosion**, and a decrease in **forest products**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Overgrazing (हरे जंगल में चरना)** by livestock in forest areas can destroy young saplings and seedlings, preventing the **natural regeneration** of the forest. It also leads to **soil compaction**, which hinders future plant growth. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Burning forests (जंगलों को जलाना)**, whether through intentional clearing or uncontrolled **forest fires**, results in the immediate destruction of **flora and fauna**, loss of **biodiversity**, and the release of massive amounts of **Carbon Dioxide** into the atmosphere. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Promoting afforestation helps in maintaining the **water cycle**, preventing **floods**, and providing a sustainable source of **timber** and **non-timber forest products (NTFP)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Forest Conservation Act, 1980:** This is a landmark act by the **Indian Parliament** aimed at protecting forests. It restricts the use of forest land for non-forest purposes without the prior approval of the **Central Government**.
 
• **National Forest Policy, 1988:** The main objective of this policy is to ensure **environmental stability** and maintain **ecological balance**. It set a national goal to have a minimum of **one-third (33%)** of the total land area of the country under forest or tree cover.
 
• **Social Forestry:** Launched in **1976**, this program aims at the management and protection of forests and **afforestation** on barren lands with the purpose of helping in environmental, social, and rural development.
 
• **Chipko Movement:** A famous non-violent social and ecological movement by rural villagers, particularly women, in **India** in the **1970s**, aimed at protecting trees and forests slated for government-backed logging. It originated in the **Reni village** of **Chamoli district**, **Uttarakhand**.
 
• **Forest Products:** Forests provide essential resources like **timber**, **fuelwood**, **medicinal plants**, **resins**, **gums**, and **lac**, which are vital for the livelihoods of millions of people, especially **tribal communities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon Sink:** Forests act as a major **carbon sink** by absorbing **Carbon Dioxide** during **photosynthesis**, which helps in mitigating the effects of **Global Warming** and **Climate Change**.
 
• **Reforestation vs. Afforestation:** While **Afforestation** is creating a new forest, **Reforestation** is the natural or intentional restocking of existing forests and woodlands that have been depleted, usually through deforestation.
 
• **Sustainable Forest Management (SFM):** This practice ensures that forest resources are used in a way that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of **future generations** to meet their own needs.
 
• **Biodiversity Hotspots:** Forests in India, such as the **Western Ghats** and the **Eastern Himalayas**, are recognized globally as **biodiversity hotspots** due to their high levels of **endemic species**.
